terms.comment: Of carrying something, often heavy, from one place to another (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Liv. 2.32.10: nē manūs ad ōs cibum ferrent

terms.gloss: carry about; carry (a child) in one’s arms
terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica et post Augustum (Lewis & Short); in cōmoediā Plaut., Ter.
evidence: Ter. Ad. 563: in manibus gestāvī meīs
terms.comment: The verb for carrying a small child about: in manibus gestāre.

terms.register: vōx ante et post aetātem classicam: Plaut., Phaedr. (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: ille domum glandēs excussaque mōra rubētīs portat et ārsūrīs ārida ligna focīs
phrases.english: he was carrying home acorns and blackberries shaken from the brambles, and dry wood for the fire

phrases.latin: quem ego modo puerum tantillum in manibus gestāvī meīs
phrases.english: whom only the other day I carried in my arms, a tiny little boy

phrases.latin: vēnālēs umerō fascēs portābat in urbem
phrases.english: he used to carry bundles to town on his shoulder, to sell

sources: Lewis & Short: porto · Lewis & Short: fero · Lewis & Short: gesto · Lewis & Short: bajulo
